issues.passage: Voters found the tax plan so unpalatable that they approved it without debate.
issues.why: "Found the tax plan so unpalatable" is correct, natural use of unpalatable = difficult to accept. The approved-without-debate clause is only pragmatic contradiction; it does not make the word itself a misuse. A student who knows the definition would rightly accept the wording.

fix.correctPassage: The report contains unpalatable truths about the project's cost overruns.
wrongPassages: Voters labeled the tax plan unpalatable because every provision was easy to accept and widely cheered.
Critics called the ending unpalatable for its gentle, crowd-pleasing resolution that left no one unsettled.
The compromise proved unpalatable once both parties found it entirely agreeable and signed without hesitation.

issues.passage: Critics called the ending unpalatable and recommended the film to every friend.
issues.why: "Called the ending unpalatable" correctly uses unpalatable = hard to find pleasant. Recommending the film is only ironic after-behavior; the word itself is used properly. A student who knows the definition would accept the passage as valid usage.

issues.passage: The compromise proved unpalatable to both parties, who signed it eagerly that afternoon.
issues.why: "Proved unpalatable to both parties" is correct use of unpalatable = difficult to accept. Eager signing is only situational hypocrisy; it does not turn the word into a misuse. A student who knows the definition would accept this passage.

issues.passage: He praised the proposal without qualification, then spent an hour listing its serious flaws.
issues.why: "Praised ... without qualification" is standard correct use of qualification = a limiting condition (here, praise with no reservation). Listing flaws afterward is only inconsistent behavior; the phrase itself is valid English a student who knows the word would accept.

fix.correctPassage: She accepted the praise with one important qualification about the study's small sample.
wrongPassages: The recipe called for two qualifications of oil, measured roughly by eye.
He praised the proposal without qualification by hedging every compliment with a major caveat.
The referee issued a qualification that removed the player from the rest of the match.
